subject: BlueMarble - Dedicated capacity incident and multipath fallback plan
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@blue-marble.health>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
Cc: platform@blue-marble.health
Date: 2028-07-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: sustained 503s - dedicated GPU pool (BlueMarble production)

Karthik / Redwood team,

We just started to see sustained 503s and timeouts from our production inference endpoints starting ~07:55 PDT. Traffic is otherwise normal on our side and only requests routed to the dedicated GPU pool appear to be impacted; fallbacks to hosted models are not in place for this workload. We have hundreds of in-flight sessions and several customers are seeing degraded responses.

Attached is a short snippet of the error stream (incident_log_20280729.txt). Can you confirm whether this is a cluster-level saturation or control-plane autoscaler issue? We have an upcoming marketing push and this is high priority for us. Please advise immediate mitigations and an ETA for full restore.

—Samir
Samir Khan
Platform Engineering, BlueMarble Health

+1 415 555 0192

Subject: Fwd: Urgent: sustained 503s - dedicated GPU pool (BlueMarble production)

Team — fyi, forwarding Samir's alert. Initial triage notes below.

What we've observed (first pass):
- Autoscaler for the dedicated pool attempted to spin additional nodes but several warmup tasks failed with driver timeouts.
- Visible build-up in the pool queue for long sequences; KV cache pressure appears high for a subset of models.
- We saw multiple nodes report preemption warnings in the same AZ (AZ-3) around 07:45–08:00.

Immediate recommendations (please action ASAP):
1) Evelyn/Ben: Trigger manual scale+evacuate for AZ-3 and drain affected nodes to the nearest healthy AZs. Set conservative warmup concurrency.
2) Camila: Enable prefix-based fallback routing for BlueMarble traffic to their secondary model variant (quantized) to shed peak tokens while preserving latency for critical endpoints.
3) Laura: Coordinate comms with account (Samir) and prepare a credit proposal if we exceed SLOs.

I've attached the mitigation runbook v2 for the manual steps. Use the cluster console to avoid triggering the autoscaler until we validate. I will take point on customer updates after we have a confirmed short-term fix.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: sustained 503s - dedicated GPU pool (BlueMarble production)

Karthik / all — acknowledged. Running the drain now. Quick status:
- Initiated node drain for AZ-3 (4 instances). Evacuation in progress; expected 6–9 minutes to finish ONCE warmup completes.
- Manually set warmup concurrency to 2 for the pool; starting sequential warmups to avoid simultaneous driver initialization spikes.
- Prefix-based fallback routing enabled for the two heaviest routes ("/v1/clinical/analyze", "/v1/notes/summary") pointing to quantized model variant (qm-v2).

Risk note: For sessions with long KV chains, quantized variant may return slightly different tokenization; Camila please add a short note we can send to the customer on observed deltas.

-Ben (on call with infra)
Evelyn Hart
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-07-29T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained 503s - dedicated GPU pool (BlueMarble production)

Samir — quick update and immediate mitigation steps we put in place: 

1) We manually drained the four affected nodes in AZ-3 and redistributed workloads; the queue backlog has started to reduce and we see successful warmups in AZ-1/2.
2) As a protective measure, we enabled prefix-based routing for your two heaviest endpoints to route to a lower-precision quantized variant (qm-v2) — this reduces per-token latency and KV footprint. Expect small differences in edge-case tokenization; Camila will follow up with note & short test cases.
3) We temporarily disabled autoscaler-driven parallel warmups to avoid concurrent driver initialization spikes; scaling will be re-enabled after a staged canary.
4) We're provisioning a short-term capacity buffer (2x warm spare nodes) for the next 6 hours while we monitor.

What we are doing next (post-restore):
- Full postmortem to cover root cause (investigating potential AZ-level hypervisor preemption + warmup concurrency bug).
- If SLOs are breached, we will propose a credit package — Laura will send the proposal within 24 hours.
- Engineering follow-up with a kernel-level patch and improved warmup sequencing for the runtime.

ETA: Recovering now; we expect customer-visible errors to be resolved within 15–30 minutes from now. We will keep you closely updated; sorry for the disruption and thanks for the quick heads-up.

Best,
Karthik
